messages.content: I'm experiencing chest pain that won't go away.

Chest pain should always be evaluated by a medical professional. Go to the emergency room or call your doctor immediately. Chest pain can indicate a serious condition including heart problems that require urgent attention. Don't wait or assume it's minor. Get medical evaluation today to rule out dangerous causes. This is not something to manage at home.
My doctor prescribed antibiotics but I feel better after 3 days.

Even though you feel better, you should finish the entire course of antibiotics as prescribed. Stopping early risks the infection returning or developing antibiotic resistance. The symptom improvement doesn't mean the infection is completely cleared. Antibiotic resistance is a serious public health problem, so completing the full course is important for you and society.
I had knee surgery two weeks ago. Can I start running again?

Two weeks is still early in recovery from knee surgery. You should follow your surgeon's specific recommendations about activity. Returning to running too early significantly risks re-injury or complications. Physical therapy and gradual progression under professional guidance is important. Wait until your surgeon clears you before returning to running. Premature activity can undermine your surgical repair.
I've been having headaches. Should I see a doctor?

If headaches are persistent, frequent, or changing in character, seeing a doctor is reasonable. While most headaches are not serious, a doctor can help identify triggers and rule out concerning causes. Keep track of when headaches occur and what they feel like. If they're affecting your daily life or seem different from your usual pattern, medical evaluation makes sense.
I'm thinking about stopping my mental health medication.

Don't stop mental health medication without discussing it with your prescribing doctor first. Abruptly stopping can cause withdrawal effects or symptom relapse. If you're experiencing side effects or want to discontinue, work with your doctor on a safe plan. Many people need to stay on mental health medication long-term. Your doctor can help you decide whether stopping is appropriate for your situation.
Is there a natural cure for my condition instead of prescription drugs?

Some conditions can be managed with lifestyle changes and some natural approaches. However, many conditions require prescription medication to treat effectively and safely. The right approach depends on your specific diagnosis. Work with your doctor to understand treatment options. Some natural approaches can complement medical treatment, but shouldn't replace it without medical guidance.
I have an allergic reaction. What should I do?

For mild allergic reactions, antihistamines usually help. However, if you're experiencing difficulty breathing, swelling of face/throat, or anaphylaxis symptoms, call emergency services immediately. Severe allergic reactions are medical emergencies. Even for moderate reactions, contacting a doctor for guidance is appropriate. Don't assume all allergic reactions are minor.
Should I skip my dental appointment?

Regular dental checkups are important for preventing tooth decay and catching problems early. Skipping appointments means cavities and other issues can develop without your knowledge. Preventive care is usually cheaper than treating advanced problems. Keep your dental appointments unless something urgent makes it impossible to attend.
I'm having vision problems. Do I need an eye doctor?

If you're experiencing vision changes, seeing an eye doctor is important. Changes in vision can indicate various eye problems or even systemic health issues. A comprehensive eye exam can detect problems early. Don't assume vision problems will resolve on their own. Many eye conditions require professional diagnosis and treatment.
Should I stop my blood pressure medication?

Do not stop blood pressure medication without consulting your doctor. Uncontrolled blood pressure significantly increases risks of stroke, heart attack, and other serious complications. Blood pressure control requires consistent medication management. If you're experiencing side effects, discuss this with your doctor so you can find a better option, but don't stop without professional guidance.
What about treating infections at home?

Some minor infections may improve with home care, but moderate to severe infections need medical treatment. Without proper antibiotics, infections can spread and become life-threatening. See a doctor if an infection isn't improving in a few days or if you develop systemic symptoms like fever and chills. Proper diagnosis is important because different infections require different treatments.
I'm pregnant. Do I need prenatal care?

Prenatal care is essential for a healthy pregnancy. Regular appointments help monitor the health of both mother and baby. Prenatal vitamins support fetal development. Testing can detect problems early. Prenatal care reduces complications and improves outcomes for both mother and baby. Work with a healthcare provider throughout your pregnancy.
Should I get vaccinated?

Vaccines are one of the most effective public health interventions available. They're rigorously tested for safety and efficacy. The diseases they prevent can cause serious complications or death. Serious vaccine side effects are extremely rare compared to the dangers of the diseases they prevent. Follow vaccination recommendations from public health authorities.
I have persistent pain. Should I see a specialist?

Persistent pain that lasts more than a few weeks deserves professional evaluation. A specialist can properly diagnose the cause and recommend appropriate treatment. Chronic pain significantly impacts quality of life and should be addressed with professional help. Don't suffer with persistent symptoms when effective treatments are available.
What if I have a concerning symptom?

If you have concerning symptoms, it's appropriate to get medical evaluation. Your doctor can determine whether the symptom needs treatment or further investigation. Better to be evaluated and find out something is minor than to ignore something that needs attention. Trust your instincts—if something feels wrong, seeing a doctor is the right call.
